method.how.tron: What a USDT transfer burns in TRX for energy and bandwidth, at the chain's current prices. Assumes the sender burns TRX, which is what most people do; staking TRX for energy makes it nearly free. A first transfer to a brand-new address costs about twice as much; both cases are on the network page.
method.how.ethereum: The gas one USDT transfer uses (measured live) × the current gas price, which is the base fee plus the tip most people are paying right now. The fast case uses a higher tip.
method.how.solana: The base fee plus the tip most people are paying, for the compute a token transfer needs. Sending to a wallet that has never held the token also pays the token-account rent, which is only refunded if that account is closed later.
method.how.bsc: The gas one USDT transfer uses (measured live) × the current gas price, which is the base fee plus the tip most people are paying right now.
method.how.polygon: The gas one USDT transfer uses (measured live) × the current gas price, which is the base fee plus the tip most people are paying right now.
method.how.arbitrum: Same as Ethereum, but the live gas estimate on Arbitrum already includes the cost of posting the transaction's data to Ethereum.
method.how.ton: The median of the total fees paid by recent real USDT transfers on the chain. Wallets also attach about 0.05 TON with each transfer, most of which comes back.
method.how.bitcoin: The fee rate for the next block, for about 30 minutes and for about 60 minutes, × the size of a typical transaction. Exchanges credit a deposit after 1 to 2 confirmations, so add 10 to 20 minutes.
method.usd_text: Fee in USD = fee in the coin × the coin's USD price (CoinGecko, cached 5 minutes; Binance and OKX prices as fallbacks). Time to credit = the confirmations big exchanges wait for × the chain's block time.
method.api_method: Read from the exchange's API every 6 hours
method.manual_method: Checked by hand against the exchange's fee page; each row shows the date
method.validation_1: No negative fees; each network has a sanity cap; a price older than one hour is rejected.
method.validation_2: A network fee more than 10× its 7-day median is treated as a glitch: the previous value is kept, marked stale, and we are alerted.
method.validation_3: If a source fails, the page keeps its last good value with the time it was seen. One broken source never takes the site down.
method.validation_4: Every exchange's network name is mapped to one internal id; unknown names are never published.
method.limits_1: Network fees are for one standard transfer at the moment shown; your wallet may pick a different priority.
method.limits_2: Exchange fees can change without notice. API values are at most 6 hours old; hand-checked values show their date.
method.limits_3: Licensing and funding facts are checked by hand against the regulator or the exchange; each row shows when.
